subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What aspects of their experience are Yelp reviewers talking about?

judge.implied_focus: Aspect-based decomposition of the Yelp dining experience (service, food/product quality, and value/pricing) with per-aspect sentiment and sub-dimension detail

per_column.name: service_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Captures sentiment toward the service aspect -- a core experiential facet reviewers discuss.

per_column.name: service_failure_type
per_column.rationale: Drills into specific service problems (rude, slow, inattentive), giving actionable granularity within the service facet.

per_column.name: food_product_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Sentiment toward the food/product aspect, a second coherent experiential facet.

per_column.name: product_quality_dimension
per_column.rationale: Decomposes food quality into flavor, temperature, portion, freshness -- a well-differentiated sub-facet structure.

per_column.name: value_pricing_sentiment
per_column.rationale: Sentiment toward the value/price aspect, completing a standard aspect trio for dining reviews.

judge.rationale: The columns centre tightly on one coherent, data-inferable focus: aspect-based analysis of the dining experience. They cover three canonical experiential aspects (service, food, value) and pair a sentiment column with a categorical sub-dimension column for two of them (failure_type, quality_dimension), yielding a genuine two-level analytical structure rather than a single restatement or generic noise. This directly answers 'what aspects are reviewers talking about' and lets an analyst quantify which aspects drive positive/negative experience and why. Minor gaps: value/pricing lacks a parallel sub-dimension column, and other plausible aspects (ambiance/atmosphere, cleanliness, wait/reservation) are absent, slightly narrowing full coverage of 'aspects of experience' -- but the realised set is disciplined, differentiated, and clearly actionable.
